Web design in New Braunfels, TX has to win a decision that happens before the customer gets here. Visitors pick the lodging from home, choose the outfitter on the drive down and settle on dinner from the river bank. Meanwhile a fast-growing population of residents searches for plumbers, dentists and daycares the same way. Dominion Web Design Pro builds a free demo of your site first, written for your business and your customers, so you can see it before you pay.

Two economies in one town

New Braunfels sits where the Comal River meets the Guadalupe, and for generations it has run on water recreation, German heritage, festivals and the visitors they bring. That trade is still huge. What has changed is the other economy: the people who live here year round.

The U.S. Census Bureau counted 90,403 residents in 2020 and estimated 110,958 by mid-2023. The city's own financial report notes that its growth since 2010, about 92 percent, has been more than three times the rate of the wider San Antonio and New Braunfels metro area.

So a New Braunfels business usually serves one of two very different searchers. The visitor wants to know what it costs and whether it is open today. The new resident wants someone reliable to come back to for years. The website has to be built for the right one.

What a tourism-facing site has to answer

Visitors ask the same handful of questions and abandon the sites that will not answer them. Most local sites open with a paragraph about the owner's passion instead. The passion matters. It belongs further down.

What does it cost?

A price, a range or a "from" figure. Visitors comparing tube rentals or tours will not call to ask.

Are you open today?

Today's hours, not general ones, and a clear note when the season changes.

Do I need to book?

A booking link or a plain "walk-ins welcome," so nobody drives over and gets turned away.

Where do I park?

On a summer Saturday near the rivers, this question decides more visits than the menu does.

Is it right for kids?

Age limits, life jacket rules, high chairs, strollers. Families check before they come.

What if it rains?

Refund and reschedule policy in one sentence, easy to find.

Where you are in town shapes what your pages need to say.

AreaTypical businessesWhat the site should lead with
Gruene Historic DistrictRestaurants, shops, music venues, lodgingEvents, hours, reservations, parking
Downtown and the Main PlazaCafes, boutiques, bakeries, professional officesLocation, hours, what makes you different
The Comal and Guadalupe river areasOutfitters, tube rentals, shuttles, snack standsPrices, booking, river conditions, parking
I-35, Creekside and SH 46Medical offices, auto service, retail, restaurantsWhich exit, open now, how to book
The newer neighborhoodsHome services, daycares, fitness, pet careService area, quotes, reviews, licensing where it applies

Gruene, inside the city limits, is home to Gruene Hall, often described as the oldest continuously operating dance hall in Texas, and it draws its own crowd of visitors who search for a place to eat or stay nearby. Wurstfest and the summer river season do the same thing for the whole town. A business that is easy to find on those weekends can earn a large share of its year in a few weeks.

Seasonal hours deserve their own warning

Nothing costs a tourism business more than a website still showing last summer's schedule. A family drives in from Houston, finds the doors locked, and leaves a one-star review that sits on your listing for years.

If your hours change through the year, keep them in one obvious place on the site and on your Google Business Profile, and update both on the same day. On a Dominion site, updates are part of hosting and maintenance, so a text or an email to Maurice is enough. The hard part is remembering, so put it on the calendar when each season starts.

For the residents' side: a plumber's site, for example

The tourism trade gets the attention, but a big share of New Braunfels businesses never see a tuber. A plumbing company serving the new subdivisions has a completely different job for its website.

  1. Lead with emergenciesA burst pipe on a Sunday is when most people meet their plumber. Put the phone number and "we answer any hour" up top if it is true.
  2. One page per job typeWater heaters, drain cleaning, slab leaks, new construction. Each answers the questions homeowners ask about that job.
  3. Say where you goNew Braunfels, Canyon Lake, Seguin, Schertz, Garden Ridge: whichever you really serve, named plainly.
  4. Show the licenseTexas plumbers are licensed by the state. Put your license number on the site where people can see it.
  5. Show real workPhotos from local jobs, and your Google reviews once you have them, displayed on the site with the Pro package.

None of that is glamorous, and that is the point. A homeowner with water on the kitchen floor is not browsing. They want to know you serve their street, that you are licensed, and how fast you can get there.

Our web design for plumbers page goes deeper on this, and the same thinking works for electricians, HVAC and roofing.

Business support in New Braunfels

The Greater New Braunfels Chamber of Commerce is one of the partners behind the New Braunfels Economic Development Corporation, along with the City of New Braunfels, Comal County, the Greater New Braunfels Economic Development Foundation and New Braunfels Utilities. A 2019 Texas Senate resolution credited the chamber with creating and supporting the local Small Business Development Center. The chamber also names a Small Business Person of the Year, open to owners with fewer than 50 employees who have run their business for at least five years.

SCORE mentors are available at no cost, and the Texas State University SBDC network serves the region. We have no connection to any of these groups. They are worth a call before you spend money with anyone.

Common questions

What do tourists look for on a New Braunfels business website?

Price, today's hours, whether they need to book, where to park, how long it takes, whether it suits kids, and what happens if it rains. A visitor with four tabs open drops the site that does not answer, so put those answers near the top.

How much does a website cost in New Braunfels, TX?

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites for $497 (Starter, 5 pages), $997 (Pro, 10 pages plus 10 city pages and a photo gallery) or $1,997 (Agency), all one time. Hosting and maintenance are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent. Compare with the typical market in our web design packages guide.

How do I keep seasonal hours current on my website?

Put your hours in one obvious place on the site and on your Google Business Profile, and change both on the same day. With Dominion Web Design Pro, updates are part of hosting and maintenance, so a quick email or text is enough. The real rule is to actually do it every time your season changes.

Do you have an office in New Braunfels?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely. You see a free demo by link, talk by phone and approve pages by email. Many New Braunfels owners already run their bookings and suppliers the same way.
